Recall is k/n with a Wilson 95% interval (a count when there are fewer than 40 cases). Versions (all evaluated on the same recorded claim scopes): v2 = before the recall work; v3 = non-penalty shot_spam, trailing box-entry share and the full-time tilt window; v4 = v3 plus the chaser-threat condition (the current code). Seeds 2026-2028 were used to choose the changes; 2029-2030 are the hold-out.

notes.heading: Reading these numbers
notes.text: field_tilt_with_lead on one full-match claim per team: 0.62 [0.49-0.73], n=60 on the tuning seeds 2026-2028, but 0.42 [0.29-0.57], n=45 on the hold-out seeds 2029-2030. The changes (including the chaser-threat line at the league's 75th percentile) were chosen on the tuning seeds, so the hold-out figure is the honest one for this level.

notes.heading: Reading these numbers
notes.text: The same rule in the Analyst pipeline, the figure users experience: 0.90 [0.80-0.95], n=60 (tuning) and 0.82 [0.69-0.91], n=45 (hold-out). The pipeline proposes a field tilt claim for every 30-minute window above 60% tilt, several per match, and a case counts as caught when any of them fires, so a window the rule misses is often caught by a neighbouring one. A full-match claim has one chance, its box-entry and threat figures are averaged over the whole match, and the league's threat line for full matches is tighter than for 30-minute windows (less spread: 1.06-1.09 against 1.29-1.37 on these leagues).
